<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="104.189.10.69" />{{GHGcorrected}}</noinclude><section begin="par45" />the abstract verbal idea, without regard to the subject or object of the action. It stands most frequently as an adverbial accusative with a finite verb of the same stem ({{GHGpar|113|h}}–s).<ref>The terms ''absolute'' and ''construct'' are of course not to be understood as implying that the Infin. constr. {{GHGheb|text=קְטֹל}} forms the {{GHGterm|construct state}} (see § 89) of the Infin. absol. ({{GHGheb|text=קָטוֹל}} ground-form ''qăṭâl''). In the Paradigms the ''Inf. constr.'', as the principal form, is placed before the other, under the name of Infinitive simply.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|45|b}}
The flexibility and versatility of the Infin. constr. and the rigidity and inflexibility of the Infin. absol. are reflected in their vocalization. The latter has unchangeable vowels, while the ''ō'' of the Infin. constr. may be lost. For {{GHGheb|text=קְטֹל}}, according to {{GHGpar|84|e|a}}, goes back to the ground-form ''qŭṭŭl''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|45|c}}
Other forms of the Infin. constr. Qal of the strong verb are—

(''a'') {{GHGheb|text=קְטַל}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=שְׁכַב|translate=to lie}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=34|verse=7}}; {{GHGheb|text=שְׁפַל|translate=to sink}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=12|verse=4}}; especially with verbs which have ''ă'' in the second syllable of the Imperf.: hence sometimes also with those, whose second or third radical is a guttural (frequently besides the ordinary form). All the examples (except {{GHGheb|text=שְׁכַב}}, see above) occur in the closest connexion with the following word, or with suffixes (see {{GHGpar|61|c}}). In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=21|verse=33}} the Masora seems to treat {{GHGheb|text=לְטֶ֫בַח}} (verse 20, in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=לְטָבַח}}) as an Infinitive={{GHGheb|text=לִטְבֹּחַ}}; probably {{GHGheb|text=לַטֶ֫בַח}} should be read.

{{GHGmargin-letter|45|d}}
(''b'') {{GHGheb|text=קַטְלָה}} and, attenuated from it, {{GHGheb|text=קִטְלָה}}; {{GHGheb|text=קָטְלָה}} and {{GHGheb|text=קֻטְלָה}} (which are feminine forms<ref>According to the remark of Elias Levita on Qimḥi’s {{GHGcite|title=Mikhlol}}, ed. Rittenb., 14 ''a'', these feminine forms occur almost exclusively in connexion with the preposition {{GHGheb|text=לְ}}.</ref> of {{GHGheb|text=קְטַל}} and {{GHGheb|text=קְטֹל}}, mostly from intransitive verbs, and sometimes found along with forms having no feminine ending in use), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=לְאַשְׁמָה|translate=to be guilty}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=5|verse=26}}, {{GHGheb|text=אַֽהֲבָה|translate=to love}}, {{GHGheb|text=שִׂנְאָה|translate=to hate}}; {{GHGheb|text=לְיִרְאָה}}, often in Dt., ''to fear''; {{GHGheb|text=זִקְנָה|translate=to be old}}; {{GHGheb|text=קִרְאָה|translate=to meet}} (in {{GHGheb|text=לִקְרַאת}} {{GHGpar|19|k}}); {{GHGheb|text=לְרִבְעָה|translate=to lie down}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=20|verse=16}}; {{GHGheb|text=לְמָשְׁחָה|translate=to anoint}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=29|verse=29}}; {{GHGheb|text=לְרָחְצָה|translate=to wash}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=30|verse=18}}, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=לְטָמְאָה}} (also a subst.= ''uncleanness'', like {{GHGheb|text=טֻמְאָה}}) ''to be unclean'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=15|verse=32}}; {{GHGheb|text=לְקָרְבָה|translate=to approach}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=36|verse=2}}, &c.; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=12|verse=4.5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=11|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=30|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=21|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hag|chapter=1|verse=6}}; also {{GHGheb|text=רָֽחֳקָה|translate=to be far off}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=8|verse=6}}; {{GHGheb|text=חֻמְלָה|translate=to pity}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=16|verse=5}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=7|verse=4}}. On the other hand in {{GHGheb|text=חֶמְלָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=16}}, the original ''ă'' has been modified to ''ĕ''; cf. {{GHGheb|text=חֶזְקָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=8|verse=11}}, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|45|e}}
(''c'') In the Aramaic manner ({{GHGheb|text=מִקְטַל}} but cf. also Arab. ''maqtal'') there occur as ''Infin. Qal'': {{GHGheb|text=מִשְׁלוֹחַ|translate=to send}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=9|verse=19}}; {{GHGheb|text=מִקְרָא|translate=to call}} and {{GHGheb|text=מַסַּע|translate=to depart}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=10|verse=2}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=10|verse=11}}); {{GHGheb|text=מִקַּח|translate=to take}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=19|verse=7}}, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=מַשָּׂא|translate=to carry}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=4|verse=24}}, &c. (cf. even {{GHGheb|text=לְמַשְׂאוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=17|verse=9}}); also with a feminine ending {{GHGheb|text=מַֽעֲלָה|translate=to go up}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=7|verse=9}}, &c.; cf. for these forms (almost all very late) Ryssel, ''De Elohistae Pentateuchici sermone'', p. 50, and Strack on {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=4|verse=24}}. {{:Gesenius' Hebrew Grammar/Additions and Corrections/123}}

(''d'') {{GHGheb|text=קְטֹ֫לֶת}} in {{GHGheb|text=יְב֫שֶׁת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=8|verse=7}}; {{GHGheb|text=יְכֹ֫לֶת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=14|verse=16}}; probably also {{GHGheb|text=חֲר֫שֶׁת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=31|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=35|verse=33|hidebook=1}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|45|f}}
'''2.''' A kind of ''Gerund'' is formed by the ''Infin. constr.'' with the preposition {{GHGheb|text=לְ}}; as {{GHGheb|text=לִקְטֹל|translate=ad interficiendum}}, {{GHGheb|text=לִנְפֹּל|translate=ad cadendum}} (see {{GHGpar|28|a}}).
